stemMd: Complete combustion of a hydrocarbon in excess oxygen produces which main products?
explanationMd: A hydrocarbon supplies carbon and hydrogen. Under complete combustion, carbon is oxidized to carbon dioxide and hydrogen to water. Excess oxygen supports complete oxidation; insufficient oxygen can instead produce carbon monoxide or soot.

distractorRationale.a: The reactants supply no sodium or chlorine.
distractorRationale.d: A pure hydrocarbon and oxygen supply no nitrogen.
distractorRationale.e: Those are associated with incomplete rather than complete combustion.
distractorRationale.b: Complete oxidation converts hydrogen to water.
